sanskrit: guruṃ pravyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā duryodhanaḥ svayam drauṇāyaniś ca saṃkruddhau bhīmasenam abhidrutau
english: Seeing the teacher sorely afflicted, King Duryodhana himself and the son of Droṇa, both in fury, rushed upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tāv āpatantau saṃprekṣya kālāntakayamopamau bhīmaseno mahābāhur gadām ādāya satvaraḥ
english: Beholding the two of them bearing down upon him, like Death and Yama at the end of time, the mighty-armed Bhīmasena swiftly seized his mace.

sanskrit: avaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ tasthau girir ivācalaḥ samudyamya gadāṃ gurvīṃ yamadaṇḍopamāṃ raṇe
english: Leaping down at once from his chariot, he stood unmoving as a mountain, raising aloft in battle his heavy mace, like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā kailāsam iva śṛṅgiṇam kauravo droṇaputraś ca sahitāv abhyadhāvatām
english: Seeing him with mace upraised, like Kailāsa with its peak, the Kaurava and the son of Droṇa together charged upon him.

sanskrit: tāv āpatantau sahitau tvaritau balināṃ varau abhyadhāvata vegena tvaramāṇo vṛkodaraḥ
english: As those two foremost among the strong rushed on together in haste, Vṛkodara too, hurrying, ran toward them with great speed.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya saṃkruddhaṃ bhīmadarśanam samabhyadhāvaṃs tvaritāḥ kauravāṇāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Beholding him bearing down, enraged and terrible to look upon, the great chariot-warriors of the Kauravas swiftly ran to meet him.

sanskrit: bhāradvājamukhāḥ sarve bhīmasenajighāṃsayā nānāvidhāni śastrāṇi bhīmasyorasy apātayan sahitāḥ pāṇḍavaṃ sarve pīḍayantaḥ samantataḥ
english: All of them, with the son of Bharadvāja at their head, in their desire to slay Bhīmasena, let fall weapons of every kind upon Bhīma's breast, and together oppressed the Pāṇḍava on every side.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃśayaṃ prāptaṃ pīḍyamānaṃ mahāratham abhimanyuprabhṛtayaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ abhyadhāvan parīpsantaḥ prāṇāṃs tyaktvā sudustyajān
english: Seeing that great chariot-warrior brought into peril and hard pressed, the great warriors of the Pāṇḍavas led by Abhimanyu rushed to his rescue, casting aside life so hard to cast away.

sanskrit: anūpādhipatiḥ śūro bhīmasya dayitaḥ sakhā nīlo nīlāmbudaprakhyaḥ saṃkruddho drauṇim abhyayāt spardhate hi maheṣvāso nityaṃ droṇasutena yaḥ
english: The valiant lord of the Anūpas, the dear friend of Bhīma, Nīla, dark as a rain-cloud, in fury fell upon the son of Droṇa — that mighty archer who ever vied with Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: sa visphārya mahac cāpaṃ drauṇiṃ vivyādha patriṇā yathā śakro mahārāja purā vivyādha dānavam
english: Drawing his great bow, he pierced the son of Droṇa with a feathered shaft, even as Śakra in olden days, O great king, pierced the Dānava —

sanskrit: vipracittiṃ durādharṣaṃ devatānāṃ bhayaṃkaram yena lokatrayaṃ krodhāt trāsitaṃ svena tejasā
english: Vipracitti, hard to assail, terror of the gods, by whom in his wrath the three worlds were affrighted through his own splendor.

sanskrit: tathā nīlena nirbhinnaḥ sumukhena patatriṇā saṃjātarudhirotpīḍo drauṇiḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ
english: Thus pierced by Nīla with a keen-pointed winged shaft, and with his blood gushing forth, the son of Droṇa was filled with wrath.

sanskrit: sa visphārya dhanuś citram indrāśanisamasvanam dadhre nīlavināśāya matiṃ matimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Drawing his wondrous bow, loud as the thunderbolt of Indra, that foremost of the wise set his mind upon the destruction of Nīla.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhāya vimalān bhallān karmārapāyitān jaghāna caturo vāhān pātayām āsa ca dhvajam
english: Then, fitting to his bow bright broad-headed arrows tempered by the smith, he slew his four steeds and brought down his banner.

sanskrit: saptamena ca bhallena nīlaṃ vivyādha vakṣasi sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopastha upāviśat
english: And with a seventh broad-headed shaft he pierced Nīla in the breast; sorely wounded and in anguish, he sank down upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: mohitaṃ vīkṣya rājānaṃ nīlam abhracayopamam ghaṭotkaco 'pi saṃkruddho bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Seeing King Nīla, dark as a mass of clouds, swooning away, Ghaṭotkaca too, in fury, surrounded by his brothers,

sanskrit: abhidudrāva vegena drauṇim āhavaśobhinam tathetare abhyadhāvan rākṣasā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: rushed with speed upon the son of Droṇa, splendid in battle; and likewise the other Rākṣasas, frenzied in war, charged after him.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya rākṣasaṃ ghoradarśanam abhyadhāvata tejasvī bhāradvājātmajas tvaran
english: Beholding that Rākṣasa of fearful aspect bearing down upon him, the splendid son of Bharadvāja swiftly rushed to meet him.

sanskrit: nijaghāna ca saṃkruddho rākṣasān bhīmadarśanān yo 'bhavann agrataḥ kruddhā rākṣasasya puraḥsarāḥ
english: And in his wrath he slew the terrible-looking Rākṣasas who, enraged, stood foremost as the vanguard of the Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: vimukhāṃś caiva tān dṛṣṭvā drauṇicāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ akrudhyata mahākāyo bhaimasenir ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Seeing them turned away by the arrows loosed from the bow of Droṇa's son, the huge-bodied Ghaṭotkaca, son of Bhīmasena, blazed up in anger.

sanskrit: prāduścakre mahāmāyāṃ ghorarūpāṃ sudāruṇām mohayan samare drauṇiṃ māyāvī rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: That lord of Rākṣasas, master of illusion, conjured up a great magic, terrible of form and most dreadful, bewildering the son of Droṇa in the fray.

sanskrit: tatas te tāvakāḥ sarve māyayā vimukhīkṛtāḥ anyonyaṃ samapaśyanta nikṛttān medinītale viceṣṭamānān kṛpaṇāñ śoṇitena samukṣitān
english: Then all your warriors, turned to flight by that illusion, beheld one another lying hewn upon the earth, writhing in piteous plight and drenched with blood —

sanskrit: droṇaṃ duryodhanaṃ śalyam aśvatthāmānam eva ca prāyaśaś ca maheṣvāsā ye pradhānāś ca kauravāḥ
english: Droṇa, Duryodhana, Śalya, and Aśvatthāman, and for the most part the great archers and the chief among the Kauravas.

sanskrit: vidhvastā rathinaḥ sarve gajāś ca vinipātitāḥ hayāś ca sahayārohā vinikṛttāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: All the chariot-warriors seemed shattered, the elephants struck down, and the horses with their riders cut to pieces by the thousand.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ vidrutaṃ śibiraṃ prati mama prākrośato rājaṃs tathā devavratasya ca
english: Seeing this, your army fled toward the camp, O king, while I and Devavrata cried aloud to them —

sanskrit: yudhyadhvaṃ mā palāyadhvaṃ māyaiṣā rākṣasī raṇe ghaṭotkacaprayukteti nātiṣṭhanta vimohitāḥ naiva te śraddadhur bhītā vadator āvayor vacaḥ
english: "Fight on, do not flee! This is but Rākṣasa illusion wrought in battle by Ghaṭotkaca!" — yet, bewildered, they would not stand their ground, nor in their terror did they heed the words of us two as we spoke.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca pradravato dṛṣṭvā jayaṃ prāptāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ ghaṭotkacena sahitāḥ siṃhanādān pracakrire śaṅkhadundubhighoṣāś ca samantāt sasvanur bhṛśam
english: Seeing them in full flight, the Pāṇḍavas, victorious now, together with Ghaṭotkaca raised lion-roars, and the blare of conches and the boom of drums resounded loudly on every side.

sanskrit: evaṃ tava balaṃ sarvaṃ haiḍimbena durātmanā sūryāstamanavelāyāṃ prabhagnaṃ vidrutaṃ diśaḥ
english: Thus, at the hour of the sun's setting, all your host was broken by the wicked son of Hiḍimbā and scattered to the quarters.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin mahati saṃkrande rājā duryodhanas tadā gāṅgeyam upasaṃgamya vinayenābhivādya ca
english: Saṃjaya said: In that great tumult of battle, King Duryodhana then drew near to the son of Gaṅgā, and bowing to him with reverence,

sanskrit: tasya sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam ākhyātum upacakrame ghaṭotkacasya vijayam ātmanaś ca parājayam
english: he began to recount to him all that had passed — the victory of Ghaṭotkaca and his own defeat.

sanskrit: kathayām āsa durdharṣo viniḥśvasya punaḥ punaḥ abravīc ca tadā rājan bhīṣmaṃ kurupitāmaham
english: The unconquerable one told his tale, sighing again and again, and then, O king, he spoke to Bhīṣma, the grandsire of the Kurus:

sanskrit: bhavantaṃ samupāśritya vāsudevaṃ yathā paraiḥ pāṇḍavair vigraho ghoraḥ samārabdho mayā prabho
english: "Relying upon you, even as the foe rely upon Vāsudeva, I have begun this terrible strife with the Pāṇḍavas, O lord.

sanskrit: ekādaśa samākhyātā akṣauhiṇyaś ca yā mama nideśe tava tiṣṭhanti mayā sārdhaṃ paraṃtapa
english: The eleven armies that are reckoned mine stand, together with me, under your command, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bharataśārdūla bhīmasenapurogamaiḥ ghaṭotkacaṃ samāśritya pāṇḍavair yudhi nirjitaḥ
english: Yet I, O tiger of the Bhāratas, have been vanquished in battle by the Pāṇḍavas led by Bhīmasena, who took Ghaṭotkaca for their stay.

sanskrit: tan me dahati gātrāṇi śuṣkavṛkṣam ivānalaḥ tad icchāmi mahābhāga tvatprasādāt paraṃtapa
english: This burns my limbs as fire burns a withered tree. Therefore I desire, O illustrious one, by your grace, O scorcher of foes,

sanskrit: rākṣasāpasadaṃ hantuṃ svayam eva pitāmaha tvāṃ samāśritya durdharṣaṃ tan me kartuṃ tvam arhasi
english: to slay that vile Rākṣasa myself, O grandsire, with you for my refuge, unconquerable one — this you ought to grant me to do."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ rājño bharatasattama duryodhanam idaṃ vākyaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt
english: Hearing this speech of the king, O best of the Bhāratas, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu spoke these words to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājan mama vaco yat tvā vakṣyāmi kaurava yathā tvayā mahārāja vartitavyaṃ paraṃtapa
english: "Hear my word, O king, which I shall speak to you, O Kaurava — how you ought to bear yourself, O great king, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: ātmā rakṣyo raṇe tāta sarvāvasthāsv ariṃdama dharmarājena saṃgrāmas tvayā kāryaḥ sadānagha
english: Your own self must be guarded in battle, dear son, in every plight, O subduer of foes; your warfare, O ever sinless one, should be waged against the King of Righteousness,

sanskrit: arjunena yamābhyāṃ vā bhīmasenena vā punaḥ rājadharmaṃ puraskṛtya rājā rājānam ṛcchati
english: or with Arjuna, or the twins, or again with Bhīmasena; for, observing the duty of kings, a king should meet a king in combat.

sanskrit: ahaṃ droṇaḥ kṛpo drauṇiḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ śalyaś ca saumadattiś ca vikarṇaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: I, and Droṇa, Kṛpa, the son of Droṇa, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas, and Śalya, and the son of Somadatta, and Vikarṇa the great chariot-warrior,

sanskrit: tava ca bhrātaraḥ śūrā duḥśāsanapurogamāḥ tvadarthaṃ pratiyotsyāmo rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahābalam
english: and your valiant brothers led by Duḥśāsana — we shall fight for your sake against that mighty Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tasmin raudre rākṣasendre yadi te hṛcchayo mahān ayaṃ vā gacchatu raṇe tasya yuddhāya durmateḥ bhagadatto mahīpālaḥ puraṃdarasamo yudhi
english: But if you cherish a great longing in your heart against that fierce lord of Rākṣasas, then let King Bhagadatta, the equal of Purandara in battle, go forth to fight that evil-minded one in the fray."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā rājānaṃ bhagadattam athābravīt samakṣaṃ pārthivendrasya vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Having said so much to the king, that master of speech then addressed Bhagadatta in the presence of the lord of kings:

sanskrit: gaccha śīghraṃ mahārāja haiḍimbaṃ yuddhadurmadam vārayasva raṇe yatto miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām rākṣasaṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ yathendras tārakaṃ purā
english: "Go swiftly, O great king, and check in battle the war-frenzied son of Hiḍimbā, striving with all your might before the eyes of all the bowmen — that Rākṣasa of cruel deeds, even as Indra of old checked Tāraka.

sanskrit: tava divyāni cāstrāṇi vikramaś ca paraṃtapa samāgamaś ca bahubhiḥ purābhūd asuraiḥ saha
english: Yours are celestial weapons and prowess too, O scorcher of foes, and in days gone by you have met in combat with many Asuras.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tasya rājaśārdūla pratiyoddhā mahāhave svabalena vṛto rājañ jahi rākṣasapuṃgavam
english: You, O tiger among kings, are his match in the great battle; girt by your own host, O king, slay that bull among Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ bhīṣmasya pṛtanāpateḥ prayayau siṃhanādena parān abhimukho drutam
english: Hearing this word of Bhīṣma, the commander of the host, he set forth swiftly with a lion-roar straight toward the foe.

sanskrit: tam ādravantaṃ saṃprekṣya garjantam iva toyadam abhyavartanta saṃkruddhāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Beholding him rushing on, thundering like a rain-cloud, the enraged great warriors of the Pāṇḍavas advanced against him —

sanskrit: bhimaseno 'bhimanyuś ca rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ draupadeyāḥ satyadhṛtiḥ kṣatradevaś ca māriṣa
english: Bhīmasena and Abhimanyu, and the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, the sons of Draupadī, Satyadhṛti, and Kṣatradeva, O venerable one,

sanskrit: cedipo vasudānaś ca daśārṇādhipatis tathā supratīkena tāṃś cāpi bhagadatto 'py upādravat
english: the lord of the Cedis and Vasudāna, and the lord of the Daśārṇas as well; and upon all these Bhagadatta too charged with his elephant Supratīka.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam pāṇḍūnāṃ bhagadattena yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: Then there arose a battle horrible of form and dreadful between the Pāṇḍavas and Bhagadatta, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: pramuktā rathibhir bāṇā bhīmavegāḥ sutejanāḥ te nipetur mahārāja nāgeṣu ca ratheṣu ca
english: The arrows let fly by the chariot-warriors, of dread speed and well sharpened, fell, O great king, upon the elephants and the chariots.

sanskrit: prabhinnāś ca mahānāgā vinītā hastisādibhiḥ parasparaṃ samāsādya saṃnipetur abhītavat
english: And the great elephants in rut, well trained by their drivers, meeting one another, fell upon each other without fear.

sanskrit: madāndhā roṣasaṃrabdhā viṣāṇāgrair mahāhave bibhidur dantamusalaiḥ samāsādya parasparam
english: Blinded by rut and seized with rage, in that great battle they gored one another with the points of their tusks and smote with their pestle-like tusks as they closed in.

sanskrit: hayāś ca cāmarāpīḍāḥ prāsapāṇibhir āsthitāḥ coditāḥ sādibhiḥ kṣipraṃ nipetur itaretaram
english: And the horses, decked with chowries and mounted by riders with lances in hand, urged swiftly on by their riders, fell upon one another.

sanskrit: pādātāś ca padātyoghais tāḍitāḥ śaktitomaraiḥ nyapatanta tadā bhūmau śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And the foot-soldiers, struck by hosts of footmen with darts and javelins, fell then to the ground by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: rathinaś ca tathā rājan karṇinālīkasāyakaiḥ nihatya samare vīrān siṃhanādān vinedire
english: And the chariot-warriors too, O king, slaying heroes in the fray with barbed and reed-shafted arrows, sent forth their lion-roars.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe bhagadatto maheṣvāso bhīmasenam athādravat
english: While that hair-raising battle thus went on, Bhagadatta the great archer rushed upon Bhīmasena,

sanskrit: kuñjareṇa prabhinnena saptadhā sravatā madam parvatena yathā toyaṃ sravamāṇena sarvataḥ
english: upon his elephant in rut, pouring forth its ichor in seven streams, like a mountain pouring down its waters on every side,

sanskrit: kirañ śarasahasrāṇi supratīkaśirogataḥ airāvatastho maghavān vāridhārā ivānagha
english: scattering thousands of arrows as he rode upon Supratīka's head, O sinless one, like Maghavat upon Airāvata pouring down showers of rain.

sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ śaradhārābhis tāḍayām āsa pārthivaḥ parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ
english: That king smote Bhīma with streams of arrows, as a thundercloud in the rains beats upon a mountain with its torrents of water.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃkruddhaḥ pādarakṣān paraḥśatān nijaghāna maheṣvāsaḥ saṃkruddhaḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, that great archer, in his wrath slew more than a hundred of the foot-guards with showers of arrows, enraged.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā nihatān kruddho bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān codayām āsa nāgendraṃ bhīmasenarathaṃ prati
english: Seeing them slain, the mighty Bhagadatta in his fury urged his lordly elephant against the chariot of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: sa nāgaḥ preṣitas tena bāṇo jyācodito yathā abhyadhāvata vegena bhīmasenam ariṃdamam
english: That elephant, sent on by him like an arrow loosed from the bowstring, rushed with speed upon Bhīmasena, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ abhyavartanta vegena bhīmasenapurogamāḥ
english: Seeing it bearing down, the great warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, with Bhīmasena at their head, advanced against it with speed —

sanskrit: kekayāś cābhimanyuś ca draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ daśārṇādhipatiḥ śūraḥ kṣatradevaś ca māriṣa cedipaś citraketuś ca saṃkruddhāḥ sarva eva te
english: the Kekayas and Abhimanyu and all the sons of Draupadī, the valiant lord of the Daśārṇas and Kṣatradeva, O venerable one, the lord of the Cedis and Citraketu — all of them enraged.

sanskrit: uttamāstrāṇi divyāni darśayanto mahābalāḥ tam ekaṃ kuñjaraṃ kruddhāḥ samantāt paryavārayan
english: Displaying their celestial weapons of the highest order, those mighty ones in their wrath surrounded that one elephant on every side.

sanskrit: sa viddho bahubhir bāṇair vyarocata mahādvipaḥ saṃjātarudhirotpīḍo dhātucitra ivādrirāṭ
english: Pierced by many arrows, that great elephant shone forth, with the gush of its flowing blood, like a lordly mountain bright with its mineral hues.

sanskrit: daśārṇādhipatiś cāpi gajaṃ bhūmidharopamam samāsthito 'bhidudrāva bhagadattasya vāraṇam
english: And the lord of the Daśārṇas too, mounted on his own elephant huge as a mountain, rushed against the elephant of Bhagadatta.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ samare gajaṃ gajapatiḥ sa ca dadhāra supratīko 'pi veleva makarālayam
english: And that lord of elephants, Supratīka, withstood that elephant bearing down upon him in battle, as the shore withstands the ocean, the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: vāritaṃ prekṣya nāgendraṃ daśārṇasya mahātmanaḥ sādhu sādhv iti sainyāni pāṇḍaveyāny apūjayan
english: Seeing the lordly elephant of the high-souled king of the Daśārṇas thus held in check, the armies of the Pāṇḍavas applauded it, crying "Well done, well done!"

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣaḥ kruddhas tomarān vai caturdaśa prāhiṇot tasya nāgasya pramukhe nṛpasattama
english: Then the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, in his wrath, hurled fourteen javelins full at the front of that elephant, O best of kings.

sanskrit: tasya varma mukhatrāṇaṃ śātakumbhapariṣkṛtam vidārya prāviśan kṣipraṃ valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Rending its armor and its face-guard adorned with gold, they entered swiftly, as serpents enter an anthill.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito nāgo bharatasattama upāvṛttamadaḥ kṣipraṃ sa nyavartata vegataḥ
english: That elephant, sorely pierced and in anguish, O best of the Bhāratas, its rut suddenly stilled, swiftly turned and wheeled away in haste.

sanskrit: pradudrāva ca vegena praṇadan bhairavaṃ svanam sa mardamānaḥ svabalaṃ vāyur vṛkṣān ivaujasā
english: And it fled with great speed, trumpeting a fearful cry, crushing its own host as the wind in its might crushes the trees.

sanskrit: tasmin parājite nāge pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccair yuddhāyaivopatasthire
english: When that elephant was put to flight, the great warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, roaring aloud their lion-roars, drew up once more for battle.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaṃ puraskṛtya bhagadattam upādravan kiranto vividhān bāṇāñ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Then, with Bhīma at their head, they rushed upon Bhagadatta, scattering arrows of many kinds and weapons of many sorts.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ rājan saṃkruddhānām amarṣiṇām śrutvā sa ninadaṃ ghoram amarṣād gatasādhvasaḥ bhagadatto maheṣvāso svanāgaṃ pratyacodayat
english: Hearing the terrible din of those enraged and wrathful warriors bearing down, O king, Bhagadatta the great archer, his fear gone in his fury, urged his elephant on against them.

sanskrit: aṅkuśāṅguṣṭhanuditaḥ sa gajapravaro yudhi tasmin kṣaṇe samabhavat saṃvartaka ivānalaḥ
english: Goaded by the hook and the thumb, that best of elephants in battle became in that moment like the fire of universal dissolution.
